sources.note: Bibliography only; lists Stappers 1952 'Enige eigenaardigheden van het West-Kanyok' (Kongo-Overzee 18(5): 382-387) and Textes kanyok 1980.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Confirms Stappers 1952 pp. 382-387; issue 5 itself is not among the archive.org Kongo-Overzee scans (only 1952 issues 1, 2-3, 4, index).
Secondary: reports high/low/falling tones and downstep citing Stappers et al. 1980 p. 201; bibliography lists Mukash-Kalel 1982/2012/2013, Boone 1961, ALAC/Zaïre 1983; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Stappers, Leo, L. Mulaji & T. Kalela. 1980. Textes kanyok. Africana Linguistica 8 (Annales MRAC 101): 199-226. Tervuren.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Intro pp. 201-202 (Western Kanyok, chefferie de Mulundu): vowel length contrastive, vowels before NC always long, final i/u devoiced; tone notation: unmarked = high, grave = low, circumflex = falling, vertical bar = downstepped high, floating grave = 'ton descendant postérieur'. Nothing about stress / accent d'intensité.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: §1 'Sons' (p. 7) gives vowel qualities and length (â, ê, ô = long) and a few consonant notes only; no mention of accent, stress or tone anywhere in the book (a full-text search for stress/accent/tonique/ton/prononc negative).
